entry.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes. These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance.
entry.summary:
These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and Itô calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Finance (q-fin.ST, q-fin.MF, q-fin.TR, q-fin.EC) · Tags: #quant-finance #market-design #probability-stats #logic

entry.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9 The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #rust #logic

entry.title: Toward Constant-Factor Maximin Share Guarantees for Subadditive Valuations
entry.summary:
For $n$ agents and $m$ indivisible goods, an agent's maximin share (MMS) is the largest minimum bundle value she can obtain by partitioning the goods into $n$ bundles. Constant MMS approximations are known for additive, submodular, or XOS valuations, but whether such a guarantee exists for general subadditive valuations remains open. We advance this question in two directions.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #logic #agents

entry.title: Linear Equivalence of Full Weight Spectrum Cyclic Orbit Codes. We determine the linear-equivalence classes within the two families of full weight spectrum one-orbit cyclic subspace codes.
entry.summary:
We determine the linear-equivalence classes within the two families of full weight spectrum one-orbit cyclic subspace codes. This solves the second open problem posed by Castello, Polverino and Zullo [J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 212 (2025) 106005].

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #logic
